title: Colonizer agent event
description: The runner→agentd event contract of docs/protocol.md §2, plus the §6.2 memory_proposal and §6.6 finding additions, as one machine-readable document. One source of truth for three hand-kept sides (#73 item 4), only two of which this schema actually covers: the Claude Code runner (modules/agents/claude-code) is tested against the committed fixture modules/agents/claude-code/test/fixtures/events.jsonl, and the Rust harness deserialises the events it acts on into the AgentEvent enum (crates/colonizer/src/protocol.rs). The browser's hand-written AgentEventBody (web/src/types.ts) is not generated or checked from this schema: it declares every event type this schema defines, memory_proposal and finding included. jev_ladder (#475) is pure telemetry: the web types it like the rest but renders nothing. Events a subagent produced may carry the agent ref, and events stored by agentd carry seq and ts (docs/protocol.md §3); neither is part of the runner contract body, so this schema does not enumerate them. The host stamps an envelope origin onto every line it appends (docs/protocol.md §3 Origins), defined at #/$defs/origin and likewise outside every body definition. Unknown fields and unknown types must be ignored for forward compatibility (§1), which is why additionalProperties is deliberately left open.

origin.description: Envelope-only field the host stamps onto every line it appends to a colony's events.jsonl and harness.jsonl at write time (docs/protocol.md §3 Origins): which subsystem caused the line. Not part of the runner contract body, which this schema defines unchanged. The vocabulary is closed: unlike the event types (§1), a value outside it is a bug in the writer and is logged loudly, not ignored. Lines written before the field existed omit it. Exception: memory_proposal's body origin names the proposer (§6.2) and predates the envelope, so those lines are not stamped and keep the proposer's value.

agent_ref.description: The subagent that produced the event: the Task tool call that started it (docs/protocol.md §2 rules). Omitted entirely on the orchestrator's own events, never null.

name.description: The subagent type, or its task description when the type was not named.

preview.description: Markdown or HTML, rendered monospace or sandboxed (§5).

options.description: Whatever the model produced, which the runner forwards unvalidated. The model is asked for 2-4 options and UIs always add 'Other' (§2 rules), but that count is a rule for the model, not a guarantee of this wire format.

model_tokens.description: Cumulative tokens one model spent as of the last turn end.

status.description: The agent's own state machine; must be emitted on every state change. agentd emits the same shape with detail set when the runner exits (§3).

user_message.description: The echo of an accepted message. Watchdog nudges are user_message echoes whose id starts with watchdog- (§6.3).

assistant_text_delta.description: Optional streaming; the final assistant_text supersedes the deltas.

thinking.description: Optional summary of the agent's thinking.

tool_call.description: AskUserQuestion never appears here: questions travel as question events (§2 rules).

denial.description: Present when the output reads as a sandbox or colony refusal. Guidance only: it never changes is_error and never grants anything (§2).

question.description: A question that needs the user's answer; UIs always add a free-text 'Other' choice (§2 rules).

risk.description: The question's risk class (§2 rules), assigned by the runner and enforced by the Mothership's autonomy judge (§6.2b). Absent means workspace_write; a value outside the vocabulary is treated as above every ceiling and is never answered automatically.

questions.description: Forwarded as the model produced them, so it can be empty or hold fewer options than the §2 rules ask the model for.

question_answered.description: The answer travelled browser ⇄ harness ⇄ agentd ⇄ runner (§2).

turn_end.description: A turn ended. cost_usd and model_usage are cumulative for the colony; cost_usd sums only the Claude models in model_usage (keys without a '/') (§2 rules).

log.description: Runner diagnostics (stderr, routing warnings, pre-flight scan findings); agentd uses the same shape for its own (§3).

model_changed.description: The orchestrator model the session runs on (§2): announced when Claude Code's init first names it, and after each set_model command the SDK accepted. The conversation, VM and worktree stay the same across a switch.

model.description: The model in effect from the next response on, as requested and set (the CLI may substitute one unreported; the next init corrects it): a Claude alias or ID, or <provider>/<model>.

previous.description: The model announced before this one; null on the first announcement of the run.

memory_proposal.description: A proposed shared-memory note (§6.2); nothing is written inside the colony. Absent scope means repo; absent tags mean none. The mothership refuses any proposal whose origin is not the orchestrator's, before it touches a store.

origin.description: Who proposed: "orchestrator", "subagent:<name>" or "background:<name>". Absent on runners from before the field existed, which could only be the orchestrator.

finding.description: A confirmed problem outside the task (§6.6); the mothership files it as a GitHub issue because the token never enters the colony.

evidence.description: How the finding was confirmed, at most 5 000 characters; a finding without evidence is not filed.

jev_ladder.description: Jev compaction's per-chunk decisions for one compaction pass, as shadow telemetry for the harness's visibility-ladder measurement (#475): the harness grades them into the data-dir-wide jev_ladder.jsonl against rereads it observes later. Never a decision input — measurement does not change what compaction keeps or drops. applied=false marks a pass the plugin computed but did not apply (the fallback path); the harness persists nothing for it.

applied.description: Whether the pass actually rewrote the transcript. false: computed but not applied, shadow of a shadow — nothing is measured.

trigger.description: What started the pass, e.g. "auto" when the context filled.

jev_ladder_decision.description: One chunk's keep/drop decision with the plugin's own relevance scores (docs/protocol.md, Token savings).

keep_call.description: The plugin's relevance score for the tool call itself, in [0,1].

keep_result.description: The plugin's relevance score for the call's result, in [0,1].
